type:Rostral ectoderm.name: Rostral ectoderm
type:Rostral ectoderm.description: Rostral ectoderm at E7.5 represents the anterior-most portion of the embryonic ectoderm, positioned adjacent to the anterior visceral endoderm signaling center during early gastrulation. This population retains significant epiblast-like character—reflecting its recent emergence from the pluripotent epiblast—and has not yet committed to definitive neural or surface ectoderm fates. It will ultimately contribute to anterior neural structures including the forebrain and anterior surface ectoderm.

type:Cranial motor neuron.name: Cranial motor neuron
type:Cranial motor neuron.description: Cranial motor neurons are post-mitotic neurons originating from the ventral hindbrain that project axons through the cranial nerves to innervate muscles of the head, face, and pharyngeal arches, as well as visceral organs. They encompass both branchiomotor neurons (controlling jaw, facial, and pharyngeal muscles) and visceral motor neurons (parasympathetic preganglionic), and are among the earliest differentiating neuronal populations in the developing brainstem.

topLinks.explanation: Both derive from the ventral neural tube neuroepithelium, where cranial motor neurons (from the pMN/basal-plate domain) and the floor plate (the ventral-most FP domain) arise as spatially adjacent progenitor populations patterned by graded Shh from the notochord, so they share recent common ancestors within the ventral neural progenitor pool.

Both are motor neurons arising from the same ventral neural-tube progenitor program (Olig2+/Nkx6.1+ pMN domain giving rise to MNX1/Hb9+ motor neurons), differing only in axial level (hindbrain cranial vs. spinal somatic), so they share a common ventral neuroepithelial progenitor lineage.

Both are ventral CNS neuronal populations arising from the anterior neuroectoderm/neural plate under Shh-dependent basal-plate programs — cranial motor neurons from the hindbrain basal plate and hypothalamic neurons from the ventral diencephalon — reflecting a shared ventral neural progenitor origin.

Cranial motor neurons (branchiomotor/visceromotor/somatic nuclei of cranial nerves) are born directly from the ventral (pMN/Nkx6+ Olig2+) neuroepithelial progenitors of the caudal hindbrain rhombomeres r5–r8, so the two cell types are simply progenitor and differentiated derivative within the same rhombomeric neural-tube lineage.

Both are ventral CNS neurons derived from the same neuroectodermal lineage—Shh/Nkx2.1-patterned ventral neural tube progenitors (basal plate/floor-plate-adjacent neuroepithelium spanning the ventral diencephalon and hindbrain)—so their shared ancestry reflects a common neural-plate/neural-tube origin rather than distinct germ-layer sources.

subtype:Facial branchiomotor neuron.name: Facial branchiomotor neuron
subtype:Facial branchiomotor neuron.description: Facial branchiomotor neurons are motor neurons of cranial nerve VII (the facial nerve) that arise in rhombomere 4 of the developing hindbrain and innervate muscles of facial expression derived from the second branchial arch. During the stages captured here (E9.0–E10.0), these neurons are being specified and undergoing their characteristic caudal migration from rhombomere 4 to rhombomere 6. They are among the earliest differentiating motor neuron populations in the hindbrain and serve as a classic model for neuronal migration and branchiomotor circuit assembly.

subtype:Oculomotor neuron.name: Oculomotor neuron
subtype:Oculomotor neuron.description: Oculomotor neurons are somatic motor neurons of cranial nerve III (CN III), originating from ventral midbrain progenitors. They innervate the majority of extraocular muscles—including the superior, inferior, and medial recti and the inferior oblique—and are among the earliest cranial motor neurons to differentiate, consistent with their emergence at E9.5. A subset also gives rise to parasympathetic preganglionic neurons that control pupillary constriction and lens accommodation.

subtype:Trigeminal branchiomotor neuron.name: Trigeminal branchiomotor neuron
subtype:Trigeminal branchiomotor neuron.description: Trigeminal branchiomotor neurons are motor neurons of cranial nerve V that reside in the trigeminal motor nucleus of the hindbrain (rhombomeres 2–3) and innervate muscles derived from the first pharyngeal arch, most notably the muscles of mastication. They arise from ventral progenitors in the hindbrain neuroepithelium and undergo characteristic lateral migration before extending axons to their peripheral targets. In the mouse embryo, these neurons are specified between E9.0 and E10.0, consistent with the stages captured in this cluster.

subtype:Trochlear neuron.name: Trochlear neuron
subtype:Trochlear neuron.description: Trochlear neurons are the motor neurons of cranial nerve IV (the trochlear nerve), which exclusively innervates the superior oblique muscle of the eye to control downward and rotational gaze. They arise from progenitors in the ventral midbrain near the isthmus and are notable among cranial motor neurons for their dorsal axon exit and contralateral projection. These neurons appear at E9.5–E10.0, consistent with the known timing of trochlear nucleus differentiation in the mouse.

subtype:Visceral motor neuron.name: Visceral motor neuron
subtype:Visceral motor neuron.description: Visceral motor neurons are a class of cranial motor neurons that innervate visceral organs and glandular structures, mediating parasympathetic and branchiomotor functions. Arising from ventral progenitors in the hindbrain, they include populations such as the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus and nucleus ambiguus, which regulate autonomic functions including heart rate, gut motility, and airway control. Their appearance from E9.0 onward is consistent with the timing of hindbrain motor neuron differentiation in the mouse embryo.

type:Diencephalon.name: Diencephalon
type:Diencephalon.description: The diencephalon is a major subdivision of the embryonic forebrain (prosencephalon) that gives rise to the thalamus, hypothalamus, epithalamus, and pretectum. Present from E8.5 through E10.0, these progenitors represent the phase of active regionalization and neurogenesis within the caudal forebrain, positioned between the telencephalon rostrally and the midbrain caudally. As a large and transcriptionally distinct population, the diencephalon is a primary source of relay and neuroendocrine centers in the mature brain.

topLinks.explanation: Both derive from the anterior neuroepithelium of the neural plate/tube, with the diencephalon (caudal forebrain) and mesencephalon being immediately adjacent prosomeric neighbors whose progenitors share recent common ancestry within the early anterior neuroectoderm.

The diencephalon and telencephalon are both prosencephalon (forebrain) derivatives arising from a common pool of anterior neural plate/neuroectoderm progenitors, so their strong shared ancestry simply reflects their origin from the same regionalized forebrain neuroepithelium.

The eye field and diencephalon both arise from the same anterior neural plate/prosencephalic neuroectoderm, with the eye field originating as a specified domain within prospective diencephalon whose optic vesicles evaginate directly from the diencephalic wall, giving them a shared forebrain progenitor pool.

The diencephalon and midbrain are adjacent anteroposterior compartments of the neural tube that both arise from the anterior neuroectoderm (neural plate) via shared prosencephalic/mesencephalic neural progenitors, so their close ancestry reflects a common early neural-plate origin.

The hypothalamus is a ventral subdivision of the diencephalon itself, so hypothalamic neurons arise directly from diencephalic (prosomere/ventral forebrain) neuroepithelial progenitors, making them essentially a regional sublineage of the diencephalon.

type:Eye field.name: Eye field
type:Eye field.description: The eye field is a domain of the anterior neural plate specified to give rise to the eyes. It is among the earliest identifiable regions of eye development, emerging around E8.5 as a single field within the prospective forebrain neuroepithelium that subsequently splits bilaterally to form the optic vesicles. These progenitors ultimately contribute to the retina, retinal pigment epithelium, and optic stalk.

topLinks.explanation: The eye field and telencephalon both arise from the anterior neural plate/prosencephalic neuroectoderm, sharing a common forebrain progenitor pool in which the single eye field is initially specified as a medial domain contiguous with the prospective telencephalon before separating.

The eye field and diencephalon both arise from the same anterior neural plate/prosencephalic neuroectoderm, with the eye field originating as a specified domain within prospective diencephalon whose optic vesicles evaginate directly from the diencephalic wall, giving them a shared forebrain progenitor pool.

The eye field and prospective hypothalamus arise from adjacent, initially contiguous Six3/Rx-expressing progenitors in the rostral anterior neural plate (ventral prosencephalon/diencephalon), so they share a common forebrain progenitor pool that splits during optic vesicle evagination.

The eye field and the hypothalamus both arise from the anterior neural plate—specifically contiguous rostral prosencephalic (ventral diencephalic) neuroectoderm sharing Rax/Six3/Otx2+ progenitors—so their close spatial and molecular co-emergence gives them recent common ancestors.

The eye field (prospective retina/diencephalon) and midbrain neurons both derive from adjacent domains of the anterior neural plate, tracing back to a shared pool of anterior neuroectoderm progenitors specified during gastrulation.

type:Floor plate.name: Floor plate
type:Floor plate.description: The floor plate is a specialized midline signaling center located at the ventral-most region of the developing neural tube. It plays a critical role in dorsoventral patterning of the spinal cord and hindbrain by secreting morphogens that specify ventral neuronal subtypes and guide commissural axon trajectories across the midline.

topLinks.explanation: Both derive from the ventral neural tube neuroepithelium, where cranial motor neurons (from the pMN/basal-plate domain) and the floor plate (the ventral-most FP domain) arise as spatially adjacent progenitor populations patterned by graded Shh from the notochord, so they share recent common ancestors within the ventral neural progenitor pool.

Both derive from Shh⁺/Foxa2⁺/Nkx2.1⁺ ventral midline neuroepithelium, with the hypothalamus arising from the rostral (anterior) extension of the floor plate in the ventral forebrain, so they share this common ventral neural-plate progenitor pool.

Both derive from the ventral midline of the neural plate/tube — the hypothalamus arises from the rostral-most extension of the Shh+/Foxa2+ floor-plate lineage, so they share Foxa2/Shh-specified ventral midline progenitors.

Floor plate and somatic motor neurons both arise from ventral neural tube neuroepithelium, sharing a common medial/ventral neural plate progenitor pool that is Shh-patterned into the midline floor plate and the adjacent pMN (Olig2+) motor neuron domain.

Floor plate and midbrain both derive from the same dorsoventrally-patterned neural tube neuroepithelium, with midbrain (mesencephalic) floor plate arising from the ventral midline of that anterior neural plate/tube, so they share a common neuroectodermal progenitor pool.

subtype:Floor plate (anterior).name: Floor plate (anterior)
subtype:Floor plate (anterior).description: The anterior floor plate is a specialized ventral midline cell population of the developing neural tube, located in the midbrain and forebrain regions. It serves as a critical signaling center that secretes morphogens and axon guidance cues to pattern ventral neural identity and direct commissural axon trajectories. During E8.5–E10.0, the anterior floor plate plays a key role in specifying midbrain dopaminergic neuron progenitors and establishing forebrain ventral midline structures.

subtype:Floor plate (posterior).name: Floor plate (posterior)
subtype:Floor plate (posterior).description: The floor plate (posterior) comprises ventral midline cells of the developing hindbrain and spinal cord neural tube. These cells serve as a critical signaling and axon guidance center, secreting chemoattractant and chemorepellent molecules that direct commissural axon trajectories across and away from the midline. Present from E8.5 onward, this population expands as the posterior neural tube elongates during trunk and tail development.

type:Forebrain.name: Forebrain
type:Forebrain.description: Forebrain (prosencephalon) progenitors are neuroectodermal cells of the anterior neural plate that, at E8.0, are undergoing regionalization to give rise to the telencephalon and diencephalon. These progenitors are specified by anterior signaling centers that suppress posterior (caudal) fates, establishing the rostral-most identity of the developing central nervous system. They will ultimately generate the cerebral cortex, hippocampus, hypothalamus, and eyes.

type:Hindbrain.name: Hindbrain
type:Hindbrain.description: The hindbrain (rhombencephalon) is the posterior domain of the developing brain, which at E8.0 is undergoing segmentation into rhombomeres that will give rise to the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata. At this early stage, hindbrain progenitors are being specified along the anterior-posterior axis through retinoic acid signaling gradients and combinatorial transcription factor codes, distinguishing them from midbrain and spinal cord neural progenitors.

type:Hindbrain (isthmic organizer).name: Hindbrain (isthmic organizer)
type:Hindbrain (isthmic organizer).description: The isthmic organizer is a critical signaling center located at the mid-hindbrain boundary (MHB) that patterns the posterior midbrain (including the tectum) and anterior hindbrain (including the cerebellum). It functions by secreting FGF and WNT morphogens that establish concentration gradients across the MHB, orchestrating region-specific neuronal differentiation and survival. This population appears from E8.5 onward, consistent with the establishment of isthmic organizer identity shortly after neural plate formation.

topLinks.explanation: The isthmic organizer sits at the midbrain–hindbrain boundary immediately rostral to rhombomere 1, so both cell types descend from the same anterior hindbrain neuroepithelium (the rostral-most hindbrain/isthmic neural plate that the FGF8-secreting organizer itself patterns), explaining their tight shared ancestry.

The isthmic organizer forms precisely at the midbrain-hindbrain boundary, so both cell types arise from the same anterior neuroectoderm progenitor pool of the caudal midbrain/rostral hindbrain neural plate (Otx2/Gbx2 interface), explaining their shared recent ancestry.

The isthmic organizer forms at the midbrain-hindbrain boundary directly adjacent to the midbrain, so both cell types descend from the same contiguous anterior neuroectoderm/neural-plate progenitors of the mesencephalon-metencephalon region.

Both are dorsal CNS neuroectoderm derivatives that arise from the anterior neural plate/neural tube, so diencephalic (forebrain) and isthmic (midbrain–hindbrain boundary) progenitors descend from a shared anterior neuroectodermal progenitor pool during neurulation.

Both are anterior-neuroectoderm derivatives specified early from a common pool of anterior neural-plate/neural-tube progenitors, so early clones seeded before anteroposterior regionalization contribute to both the forebrain (ventral hypothalamic) and midbrain-hindbrain-boundary (isthmic organizer) domains.

type:Hindbrain (r1).name: Hindbrain (r1)
type:Hindbrain (r1).description: Hindbrain rhombomere 1 (r1) is the most anterior segment of the developing hindbrain, lying immediately caudal to the midbrain-hindbrain boundary (isthmus). This domain gives rise to the cerebellum and contributes to pontine structures, and it is patterned by signals emanating from the isthmic organizer. Present from E8.5 through E10.0, these neural progenitors are actively undergoing regionalization and early neurogenesis during this developmental window.

topLinks.explanation: The isthmic organizer sits at the midbrain–hindbrain boundary immediately rostral to rhombomere 1, so both cell types descend from the same anterior hindbrain neuroepithelium (the rostral-most hindbrain/isthmic neural plate that the FGF8-secreting organizer itself patterns), explaining their tight shared ancestry.

Midbrain and rhombomere-1 hindbrain are immediately adjacent neuroectodermal territories flanking the midbrain–hindbrain (isthmic) boundary, so they descend from a common anterior neural-plate/neural-tube progenitor pool patterned around the isthmic organizer.

Both are adjacent rhombomeric segments of the hindbrain arising from the same anterior neuroectoderm/neural plate progenitor pool, so they share recent common progenitors within the developing neural tube's hindbrain region.

Hindbrain rhombomere 1 and midbrain neurons both arise from anterior neuroectoderm progenitors flanking the midbrain-hindbrain boundary (isthmic organizer), which patterns adjacent mes/rhombencephalic neural-plate cells from a shared founder pool.

Both are neural tube derivatives arising from the common neuroectoderm/neural plate, so their shared ancestry reflects a common pool of Sox2+ neural progenitors specified along the anteroposterior neural axis before regionalization into anterior hindbrain (r1) and posterior spinal cord.

type:Hindbrain (r2-r4).name: Hindbrain (r2-r4)
type:Hindbrain (r2-r4).description: Hindbrain (r2-r4) cells are neural progenitors and early neurons arising from rhombomeres 2 through 4 of the developing hindbrain. These segments of the rhombencephalon are patterned by retinoic acid gradients and Hox gene codes, and they give rise to cranial motor neurons, sensory relay nuclei, and neural crest populations that contribute to craniofacial structures. This cluster emerges at E8.5, consistent with the onset of hindbrain segmentation, and expands through E10.0 as rhombomere-specific neuronal differentiation proceeds.

topLinks.explanation: Both cell types derive from the dorsal neural tube neuroectoderm along the anteroposterior axis, sharing progenitors in the neural plate/neural tube that generate rhombomeric hindbrain and spinal cord interneurons from a common columnar neuroepithelial lineage.

Both cell types derive from the same anterior neural plate/hindbrain neuroepithelium and are continuous, adjacent rhombomeric segments patterned along the same rostrocaudal axis, so they descend from a shared neural progenitor pool before Hox-driven rhombomere identities resolve.

Both are adjacent rhombomeric segments of the hindbrain arising from the same anterior neuroectoderm/neural plate progenitor pool, so they share recent common progenitors within the developing neural tube's hindbrain region.

Cranial motor neurons are born directly within the hindbrain neuroepithelium—rhombomeres r2–r4 host the trigeminal (V) and facial (VII) branchiomotor/visceromotor progenitors in their basal plate—so both cell types derive from the same rhombomeric neural progenitor pool.

Both are contiguous anteroposterior subdivisions of the same anterior neural tube neuroepithelium, arising from a common regional progenitor pool in the hindbrain/midbrain-hindbrain-boundary neural plate before rhombomeric segmentation partitions them.

type:Hindbrain (r5-r8).name: Hindbrain (r5-r8)
type:Hindbrain (r5-r8).description: Hindbrain (r5-r8) comprises the caudal rhombomeric segments of the developing rhombencephalon, spanning rhombomeres 5 through 8. These segments give rise to the myelencephalon (future medulla oblongata) and contribute to the caudal metencephalon, generating diverse neuronal populations including reticulospinal neurons, branchiomotor neurons of cranial nerves, and precerebellar nuclei. This population emerges at E8.5 as rhombomere boundaries become morphologically distinct and expands substantially through E10.0 as neurogenesis accelerates in the caudal hindbrain.

topLinks.explanation: Both are dorsal neural-tube derivatives arising from contiguous, caudally-adjacent domains of the posterior neural plate/tube—the r5–r8 hindbrain and cervical spinal cord emerging from the same posterior neuroectoderm (partly fed by Sox2+ neuromesodermal progenitors)—so they inherit a shared caudal CNS progenitor pool.

Both derive from the same posterior neuroepithelium of the caudal neural tube—the hindbrain (r5–r8) and adjacent spinal cord form a contiguous progenitor field patterned by shared dorsoventral (and neuromesodermal progenitor–fed) neural precursors that give rise to interneurons in both regions.

Both cell types derive from the same anterior neural plate/hindbrain neuroepithelium and are continuous, adjacent rhombomeric segments patterned along the same rostrocaudal axis, so they descend from a shared neural progenitor pool before Hox-driven rhombomere identities resolve.

Cranial motor neurons (branchiomotor/visceromotor/somatic nuclei of cranial nerves) are born directly from the ventral (pMN/Nkx6+ Olig2+) neuroepithelial progenitors of the caudal hindbrain rhombomeres r5–r8, so the two cell types are simply progenitor and differentiated derivative within the same rhombomeric neural-tube lineage.

Somatic motor neurons of the caudal hindbrain (e.g. abducens in r5–r6 and hypoglossal in r7–r8) are directly born from the ventral (pMN/Olig2+) neuroepithelial progenitors of the r5–r8 rhombomeres, so the two cell types simply reflect a progenitor-to-progeny relationship within the same hindbrain neural tube domain.

type:Hypothalamic neuron.name: Hypothalamic neuron
type:Hypothalamic neuron.description: Hypothalamic neurons are ventral forebrain neurons arising from the diencephalic floor plate that will form the nuclei of the hypothalamus, a brain region critical for homeostatic regulation including feeding, thermoregulation, and neuroendocrine signaling. These neurons begin differentiating from progenitors in the ventral diencephalon around E9.0 in the mouse, consistent with their appearance at E9.0–E10.0 in this dataset.

topLinks.explanation: Hypothalamic neurons are the differentiated neuronal progeny of the ventral diencephalic (hypothalamic) neuroepithelium, so they and the broader "hypothalamus" cell population share a direct progenitor–progeny relationship arising from the same neural-tube region.

Both derive from Shh⁺/Foxa2⁺/Nkx2.1⁺ ventral midline neuroepithelium, with the hypothalamus arising from the rostral (anterior) extension of the floor plate in the ventral forebrain, so they share this common ventral neural-plate progenitor pool.

The hypothalamus is a ventral subdivision of the diencephalon itself, so hypothalamic neurons arise directly from diencephalic (prosomere/ventral forebrain) neuroepithelial progenitors, making them essentially a regional sublineage of the diencephalon.

Both derive from the anterior neuroectoderm of the early neural plate/tube—hypothalamic neurons from the ventral diencephalon and midbrain cells from the adjacent mesencephalon—so they descend from a shared pool of spatially contiguous anterior neural progenitors that co-emerge during forebrain–midbrain regionalization.

The eye field and the hypothalamus both arise from the anterior neural plate—specifically contiguous rostral prosencephalic (ventral diencephalic) neuroectoderm sharing Rax/Six3/Otx2+ progenitors—so their close spatial and molecular co-emergence gives them recent common ancestors.

subtype:Paraventricular hypothalamic neu.name: Paraventricular hypothalamic neuron
subtype:Paraventricular hypothalamic neu.description: Paraventricular hypothalamic neurons are a neuroendocrine population arising in the developing paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of the hypothalamus, one of the principal integration centers of the neuroendocrine and autonomic nervous systems. In the mature brain these neurons produce neuropeptides such as oxytocin, vasopressin, and corticotropin-releasing hormone to regulate stress responses, fluid balance, and metabolism. Their emergence at E9.5–E10.0 is consistent with the early specification of hypothalamic neuroendocrine progenitors during diencephalic patterning.

subtype:Subthalamic nucleus neuron.name: Subthalamic nucleus neuron
subtype:Subthalamic nucleus neuron.description: The subthalamic nucleus (STN) is a glutamatergic nucleus of the ventral diencephalon that arises from the caudal hypothalamic neuroepithelium during embryonic development. It becomes a key component of the basal ganglia circuitry, serving as a major excitatory node that regulates motor control, and its dysfunction is central to the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease. These early STN neurons, appearing from E9.0 onward, represent one of the first postmitotic neuronal populations to differentiate in the developing hypothalamic-subthalamic continuum.

type:Hypothalamus.name: Hypothalamus
type:Hypothalamus.description: The hypothalamus is a ventral diencephalic structure that serves as a critical neuroendocrine and homeostatic control center in the mature brain. During E8.5–E10.0, hypothalamic progenitors are specified within the ventral forebrain neuroepithelium through the combinatorial activity of region-specific transcription factors. This cluster captures early hypothalamic progenitors and nascent neurons as they emerge from the ventral diencephalic floor.

topLinks.explanation: Hypothalamic neurons are the differentiated neuronal progeny of the ventral diencephalic (hypothalamic) neuroepithelium, so they and the broader "hypothalamus" cell population share a direct progenitor–progeny relationship arising from the same neural-tube region.

Both derive from the ventral midline of the neural plate/tube — the hypothalamus arises from the rostral-most extension of the Shh+/Foxa2+ floor-plate lineage, so they share Foxa2/Shh-specified ventral midline progenitors.

The eye field and prospective hypothalamus arise from adjacent, initially contiguous Six3/Rx-expressing progenitors in the rostral anterior neural plate (ventral prosencephalon/diencephalon), so they share a common forebrain progenitor pool that splits during optic vesicle evagination.

The hypothalamus is the ventral subdivision of the diencephalon itself, so both cell types descend from the same prosomeric diencephalic neuroepithelium (prosomeres p1–p3 of the forebrain neural plate) and inevitably share recent common progenitors.

Both the hypothalamus and telencephalon derive from the prosencephalon (anterior forebrain) of the rostral neural plate, sharing SIX3/SIX6/FOXG1-expressing anterior neuroectoderm progenitors that co-emerge during forebrain regionalization.

type:Midbrain.name: Midbrain
type:Midbrain.description: The midbrain (mesencephalon) is a major subdivision of the developing brain derived from the mesencephalic vesicle of the neural tube. In the mouse embryo from E8.0 to E10.0, midbrain progenitors undergo rapid proliferation and regional patterning, ultimately giving rise to structures such as the tectum (superior and inferior colliculi) and the tegmentum, which include dopaminergic neurons critical for motor control and reward circuits. This population represents the broad progenitor and early neuronal compartment of the midbrain across mid-to-late organogenesis stages.

topLinks.explanation: Midbrain neurons differentiate directly from midbrain neuroepithelial/neural progenitors within the mesencephalic neural tube, so the two cell types represent successive stages of a single lineage sharing recent common progenitors.

The isthmic organizer forms precisely at the midbrain-hindbrain boundary, so both cell types arise from the same anterior neuroectoderm progenitor pool of the caudal midbrain/rostral hindbrain neural plate (Otx2/Gbx2 interface), explaining their shared recent ancestry.

Midbrain and rhombomere-1 hindbrain are immediately adjacent neuroectodermal territories flanking the midbrain–hindbrain (isthmic) boundary, so they descend from a common anterior neural-plate/neural-tube progenitor pool patterned around the isthmic organizer.

The diencephalon and midbrain are adjacent anteroposterior compartments of the neural tube that both arise from the anterior neuroectoderm (neural plate) via shared prosencephalic/mesencephalic neural progenitors, so their close ancestry reflects a common early neural-plate origin.

Both derive from the anterior neuroectoderm of the early neural plate/tube—hypothalamic neurons from the ventral diencephalon and midbrain cells from the adjacent mesencephalon—so they descend from a shared pool of spatially contiguous anterior neural progenitors that co-emerge during forebrain–midbrain regionalization.

type:Midbrain neuron.name: Midbrain neuron
type:Midbrain neuron.description: Midbrain neurons are postmitotic neurons arising from the mesencephalic vesicle of the developing neural tube. During E8.5–E10.0, these cells differentiate from midbrain progenitors to populate structures that will give rise to the tectum, tegmentum, and associated nuclei. They are among the earliest neuronal populations to mature in the embryonic brain, playing roles in motor coordination, sensory relay, and dopaminergic circuitry.

topLinks.explanation: Midbrain neurons differentiate directly from midbrain neuroepithelial/neural progenitors within the mesencephalic neural tube, so the two cell types represent successive stages of a single lineage sharing recent common progenitors.

Both derive from the anterior neuroepithelium of the neural plate/tube, with the diencephalon (caudal forebrain) and mesencephalon being immediately adjacent prosomeric neighbors whose progenitors share recent common ancestry within the early anterior neuroectoderm.

The isthmic organizer forms at the midbrain-hindbrain boundary directly adjacent to the midbrain, so both cell types descend from the same contiguous anterior neuroectoderm/neural-plate progenitors of the mesencephalon-metencephalon region.

Hindbrain rhombomere 1 and midbrain neurons both arise from anterior neuroectoderm progenitors flanking the midbrain-hindbrain boundary (isthmic organizer), which patterns adjacent mes/rhombencephalic neural-plate cells from a shared founder pool.

Midbrain neurons and telencephalon both derive from the anterior neuroectoderm/neural plate, tracing back to a shared pool of early anterior neural progenitors that only later become regionalized along the antero-posterior axis into forebrain and midbrain.

subtype:Midbrain GABAergic neuron.name: Midbrain GABAergic neuron
subtype:Midbrain GABAergic neuron.description: Midbrain GABAergic neurons are inhibitory interneurons arising in the mesencephalon that utilize gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) as their primary neurotransmitter. In the E9.5–E10.0 mouse embryo, these represent early-born postmitotic neurons differentiating within the midbrain ventricular and mantle zones, contributing to nascent inhibitory circuits in structures such as the superior and inferior colliculi.

type:Roof plate.name: Roof plate
type:Roof plate.description: The roof plate is a specialized dorsal midline signaling center of the developing neural tube that secretes BMP and Wnt morphogens to pattern dorsal cell fates. It plays essential roles in specifying dorsal interneuron subtypes, guiding commissural axon trajectories, and inducing neural crest emigration from E8.5 onward as the neural tube closes along the rostrocaudal axis.

topLinks.explanation: Both cell types originate from the dorsal neural tube / neural plate border, where a shared dorsal neuroectodermal progenitor pool gives rise to premigratory trunk neural crest that delaminates and to the roof plate that remains at the dorsal midline.

Both derive from the dorsal neural tube/neural plate border, where roof plate cells and vagal neural crest arise from a shared dorsal neuroepithelial progenitor pool, with neural crest delaminating from the same dorsal domain that gives rise to the roof plate.

Cranial neural crest and roof plate both originate from the dorsal neuroepithelium/neural plate border of the anterior neural tube, where premigratory neural crest delaminates from the same dorsal progenitors that give rise to the roof plate, so they share recent common ancestors in this dorsal neural progenitor pool.

Both cell types derive from the dorsal-most neural tube / neural plate border, where premigratory trunk neural crest (which gives rise to DRG progenitors) delaminates from the same dorsal neuroepithelium that forms the roof plate, so they share a common dorsal progenitor pool.

Both derive from the dorsal-most neurectoderm/neural plate border: sacral neural crest delaminates from the dorsal neural tube whose remaining midline cells become the roof plate, so they share a common dorsal neural tube (neural plate border) progenitor pool.

subtype:Roof plate (anterior).name: Roof plate (anterior)
subtype:Roof plate (anterior).description: The roof plate (anterior) comprises the dorsal midline signaling cells of the developing brain — spanning the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain regions of the neural tube. This specialized organizer tissue secretes Wnt, BMP, and axon guidance signals that pattern dorsal CNS identity and direct commissural axon trajectories in cranial regions. Present from E8.5 onward, it emerges as the anterior neural tube closes and continues to function as a signaling center through organogenesis stages.

subtype:Roof plate (posterior).name: Roof plate (posterior)
subtype:Roof plate (posterior).description: The roof plate (posterior) comprises the dorsal midline signaling cells of the caudal (spinal cord-level) neural tube during mouse embryogenesis. These cells act as a key organizer, secreting Wnt and BMP morphogens to pattern dorsal interneuron subtypes along the trunk and tail regions. Present from E8.5 onward, they coordinate dorsoventral patterning in concert with retinoic acid signaling that establishes posterior axial identity.

type:Somatic motor neuron.name: Somatic motor neuron
type:Somatic motor neuron.description: Somatic motor neurons are post-mitotic neurons arising from the pMN progenitor domain in the ventral spinal cord and hindbrain that extend axons peripherally to innervate skeletal muscles. They are among the earliest neurons to differentiate in the developing neural tube, appearing from E9.0 onward in the mouse, and are specified by Shh-dependent ventral patterning signals. These neurons are essential for voluntary movement and serve as a classic model for understanding neuronal subtype specification.

topLinks.explanation: Somatic motor neurons are born from the pMN progenitor domain of the ventral neural tube and therefore share a direct neuroepithelial ancestry with thoracic spinal cord cells, both descending from the same posterior neural-plate/neural-tube progenitors.

Somatic motor neurons are born within the spinal cord itself, arising from Olig2+ pMN progenitors in the ventral neural tube, so they and cervical spinal cord tissue derive from the same neuroectodermal neural-tube progenitor pool.

Both are motor neurons arising from the same ventral neural-tube progenitor program (Olig2+/Nkx6.1+ pMN domain giving rise to MNX1/Hb9+ motor neurons), differing only in axial level (hindbrain cranial vs. spinal somatic), so they share a common ventral neuroepithelial progenitor lineage.

Floor plate and somatic motor neurons both arise from ventral neural tube neuroepithelium, sharing a common medial/ventral neural plate progenitor pool that is Shh-patterned into the midline floor plate and the adjacent pMN (Olig2+) motor neuron domain.

Somatic motor neurons of the caudal hindbrain (e.g. abducens in r5–r6 and hypoglossal in r7–r8) are directly born from the ventral (pMN/Olig2+) neuroepithelial progenitors of the r5–r8 rhombomeres, so the two cell types simply reflect a progenitor-to-progeny relationship within the same hindbrain neural tube domain.

type:Spinal cord.name: Spinal cord
type:Spinal cord.description: Spinal cord progenitors are neuroepithelial cells of the caudal neural plate and nascent neural tube that will give rise to the neurons and glia of the spinal cord. At E8.0, these cells reside in the posterior embryo and are actively undergoing regionalization along the anteroposterior axis through Hox gene activation and retinoic acid signaling, establishing the segmental identity that defines distinct spinal cord domains.

type:Spinal cord (cervical).name: Spinal cord (cervical)
type:Spinal cord (cervical).description: Spinal cord (cervical) cells are neural progenitors and neurons of the developing cervical spinal cord, arising from the caudal neural tube during mid-to-late embryogenesis. This population encompasses the anteroposterior domain of the spinal cord roughly corresponding to the future cervical vertebral segments, where retinoic acid signaling plays a central role in regional patterning and neuronal differentiation. Present from E8.5 through E10.0, these cells emerge as the neural tube closes and begins rostrocaudal regionalization.

topLinks.explanation: Both are dorsal neural-tube derivatives arising from contiguous, caudally-adjacent domains of the posterior neural plate/tube—the r5–r8 hindbrain and cervical spinal cord emerging from the same posterior neuroectoderm (partly fed by Sox2+ neuromesodermal progenitors)—so they inherit a shared caudal CNS progenitor pool.

Somatic motor neurons are born within the spinal cord itself, arising from Olig2+ pMN progenitors in the ventral neural tube, so they and cervical spinal cord tissue derive from the same neuroectodermal neural-tube progenitor pool.

Cervical and thoracic spinal cord are adjacent anteroposterior segments of the same neural tube generated sequentially from the shared caudal neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP)/caudal-lateral-epiblast pool, so neighboring axial levels naturally descend from common recently-specified progenitors.

Spinal cord interneurons are a differentiated neuronal subtype of the cervical spinal cord itself, both arising from the same dorsoventral neural-tube neuroepithelial (ventricular-zone) progenitors, so their shared ancestry simply reflects a part-to-whole progenitor relationship within one tissue.

Vagal neural crest delaminates from the neural-plate border/dorsal neural tube overlying somites 1–7, the same axially-restricted neuroectodermal (dorsal neural tube) progenitor domain that generates the cervical spinal cord, so both arise together from a shared cervical-level neural progenitor pool.

type:Spinal cord (lumbar).name: Spinal cord (lumbar)
type:Spinal cord (lumbar).description: Spinal cord (lumbar) cells are neural progenitors and early neurons of the caudal spinal cord corresponding to the lumbar segment, which will later innervate the hindlimb and pelvic regions. Arising from neural ectoderm between E8.5 and E10.0, these cells are actively undergoing neurogenesis and axon pathfinding as the spinal cord elongates along the anterior-posterior axis. This population represents one of the posterior-most specified domains of the developing spinal cord.

topLinks.explanation: Lumbar and sacral spinal cord are adjacent posterior neural tube segments generated sequentially from the same caudal neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP) pool in the tailbud/caudal lateral epiblast, so their close spatiotemporal co-emergence along the AP axis gives them a shared recent progenitor origin.

Sacral neural crest and lumbar spinal cord share ancestry because both are caudal derivatives of the same posterior neuroepithelium—the crest delaminating from the dorsal neural tube while the spinal cord forms its ventralized core—with their matched posterior (lumbosacral) identity seeded by common neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) in the tailbud/caudal lateral epiblast.

Lumbar and thoracic spinal cord are the same tissue at different axial levels, both generated sequentially from the same posterior neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP)/caudal neural plate pool during axis elongation, so they share recent common ancestors.

Axial progenitors (neuromesodermal progenitors, NMPs) in the caudal lateral epiblast/tailbud directly generate the posterior neural tube, so lumbar (posterior) spinal cord neurectoderm descends from this same self-renewing progenitor pool.

Presomitic (paraxial) mesoderm and lumbar spinal cord both derive from bipotent neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) in the caudal lateral epiblast/tailbud, which co-generate posterior paraxial mesoderm and posterior spinal neural tube during axis elongation.

type:Spinal cord (sacral).name: Spinal cord (sacral)
type:Spinal cord (sacral).description: Spinal cord (sacral) cells are neural progenitors and early neurons of the caudal-most specified region of the developing spinal cord, corresponding to future sacral segments. Emerging during posterior axis elongation at E9.0–E10.0, these cells arise from neuromesodermal progenitor-derived neural ectoderm and are patterned along the anteroposterior axis by a combinatorial Hox code that establishes sacral positional identity.

topLinks.explanation: Axial progenitors (neuromesodermal progenitors of the caudal lateral epiblast/tailbud) are the direct bipotent source of caudal neural tube, so sacral spinal cord neurectoderm is generated from this same Sox2/T-expressing progenitor pool, explaining their strong shared ancestry.

Lumbar and sacral spinal cord are adjacent posterior neural tube segments generated sequentially from the same caudal neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP) pool in the tailbud/caudal lateral epiblast, so their close spatiotemporal co-emergence along the AP axis gives them a shared recent progenitor origin.

Both derive from bipotent neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) in the caudal lateral epiblast/tailbud, which co-generate paraxial (presomitic) mesoderm and posterior/caudal (sacral) spinal cord neurectoderm during axial elongation.

Caudal (sacral) spinal cord and nascent somites are both generated late from the same bipotent neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) in the tailbud/caudal lateral epiblast, which co-produce posterior neural tube and paraxial mesoderm.

Sacral neural crest and sacral spinal cord both arise from the same posterior/sacral neural tube neuroepithelium—neural crest delaminates from the dorsal neural tube at matched axial levels—likely tracing back to a shared caudal neural plate (and neuromesodermal progenitor–derived) progenitor pool.

type:Spinal cord (thoracic).name: Spinal cord (thoracic)
type:Spinal cord (thoracic).description: Spinal cord (thoracic) cells are neural progenitors and early neurons of the developing spinal cord specified to thoracic axial identity. Arising from posterior neural tube closure during E8.5–E10.0, these cells give rise to the segment of spinal cord that innervates the trunk, including intercostal muscles and sympathetic ganglia. They are distinguished from other spinal cord regions by a combinatorial Hox transcription factor code that encodes positional information along the anterior-posterior axis.

topLinks.explanation: Lumbar and thoracic spinal cord are the same tissue at different axial levels, both generated sequentially from the same posterior neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP)/caudal neural plate pool during axis elongation, so they share recent common ancestors.

Somatic motor neurons are born from the pMN progenitor domain of the ventral neural tube and therefore share a direct neuroepithelial ancestry with thoracic spinal cord cells, both descending from the same posterior neural-plate/neural-tube progenitors.

Cervical and thoracic spinal cord are adjacent anteroposterior segments of the same neural tube generated sequentially from the shared caudal neuromesodermal progenitor (NMP)/caudal-lateral-epiblast pool, so neighboring axial levels naturally descend from common recently-specified progenitors.

Both cell types derive from the posterior neural tube/neural plate border — sacral neural crest delaminates from the dorsal neural tube while thoracic spinal cord forms its ventral/intermediate compartment, and both are generated by the caudal neuromesodermal progenitor pool (tailbud/CLE) that builds the posterior neuraxis, so they share a common neuroectodermal progenitor.

Trunk neural crest delaminates from the dorsal-most neuroepithelium of the closing neural tube, so it shares an immediate progenitor pool (the dorsal spinal cord neuroepithelium, itself derived from posterior neuromesodermal/neural-plate progenitors) with thoracic spinal cord neurons.

type:Spinal cord interneuron.name: Spinal cord interneuron
type:Spinal cord interneuron.description: Spinal cord interneurons are post-mitotic neurons arising within the developing spinal cord that form local circuits mediating sensory processing, motor coordination, and reflexive behaviors. In the mouse embryo from E9.0 to E10.0, these cells are actively differentiating from ventral and dorsal progenitor domains, extending axons—including commissural projections across the floor plate—and beginning to establish the spinal cord's intrinsic circuitry.

topLinks.explanation: Both derive from the same posterior neuroepithelium of the caudal neural tube—the hindbrain (r5–r8) and adjacent spinal cord form a contiguous progenitor field patterned by shared dorsoventral (and neuromesodermal progenitor–fed) neural precursors that give rise to interneurons in both regions.

Spinal cord interneurons are a differentiated neuronal subtype of the cervical spinal cord itself, both arising from the same dorsoventral neural-tube neuroepithelial (ventricular-zone) progenitors, so their shared ancestry simply reflects a part-to-whole progenitor relationship within one tissue.

Both cell types derive from the dorsal neural tube neuroectoderm along the anteroposterior axis, sharing progenitors in the neural plate/neural tube that generate rhombomeric hindbrain and spinal cord interneurons from a common columnar neuroepithelial lineage.

Both cell types arise from neuroepithelial progenitors of the ventral spinal cord (neural tube), where Shh/patterning generates adjacent progenitor domains (e.g. pMN motor neurons and p0–p3/dI interneurons) from a shared neuroectodermal pool.

Both cell types derive from the same dorsal neural tube neuroepithelial progenitors of the spinal cord, with spinal interneurons being a differentiated neuronal subtype born in situ from the thoracic spinal cord neural progenitor pool.

subtype:Dl1 interneuron.name: Dl1 interneuron
subtype:Dl1 interneuron.description: Dl1 (dI1) interneurons are a class of dorsal spinal cord interneurons that arise from the dp1 progenitor domain in the dorsal neural tube. They differentiate into commissural relay neurons that extend axons ventrally and across the midline, ultimately conveying proprioceptive and mechanosensory information to higher brain centers including the cerebellum. These neurons emerge during spinal cord neurogenesis from E9.0 onward, consistent with the stages observed here.

subtype:Dl2-6 interneuron.name: Dl2-6 interneuron
subtype:Dl2-6 interneuron.description: Dl2-6 interneurons are class B dorsal interneurons arising from progenitor domains in the dorsal half of the developing spinal cord neural tube. These postmitotic neurons, encompassing dorsal interneuron populations dI2 through dI6, are generated between E9.0 and E10.0 as the spinal cord differentiates, and they contribute to diverse somatosensory and proprioceptive relay circuits, with many projecting commissural axons across the midline.

subtype:Spinal cord interneuron progenit.name: Spinal cord interneuron progenitor
subtype:Spinal cord interneuron progenit.description: Spinal cord interneuron progenitors are actively dividing neural progenitor cells residing in the ventricular zone of the developing spinal cord that are committed to generating postmitotic interneurons. These cells occupy defined progenitor domains along the dorsoventral axis of the neural tube and undergo symmetric and asymmetric divisions to expand the interneuron pool during spinal cord neurogenesis from E9.0 onward. Upon cell cycle exit, they give rise to diverse interneuron subtypes that mediate local circuit connectivity in the spinal cord.

subtype:V0 interneuron.name: V0 interneuron
subtype:V0 interneuron.description: V0 interneurons are a class of ventral spinal cord interneurons that originate from the p0 progenitor domain, defined by expression of the transcription factor Dbx1. They are predominantly commissural neurons that project axons across the ventral midline and are essential for coordinating left-right alternation during locomotion. V0 interneurons emerge during mid-neurogenesis stages (E9.0–E10.0) as the ventral spinal cord becomes patterned along the dorsoventral axis.

subtype:V1 interneuron.name: V1 interneuron
subtype:V1 interneuron.description: V1 interneurons are an inhibitory (GABAergic/glycinergic) interneuron population of the ventral spinal cord, arising from the p1 progenitor domain under the influence of graded Sonic hedgehog signaling. They function as key components of spinal locomotor circuits, providing ipsilateral inhibitory feedback onto motor neurons to regulate the speed and coordination of limb movement. Their appearance at E9.0–E10.0 is consistent with the timing of ventral interneuron differentiation during spinal cord neurogenesis.

subtype:V2 interneuron.name: V2 interneuron
subtype:V2 interneuron.description: V2 interneurons are a cardinal class of spinal cord interneurons generated from the p2 progenitor domain during neural tube patterning. They subdivide into excitatory V2a and inhibitory V2b populations that integrate into central pattern generator circuits controlling locomotion. Appearing at E9.5–E10.0, this cluster captures V2 interneurons during their initial differentiation and early fate diversification in the developing spinal cord.

subtype:V3 interneuron.name: V3 interneuron
subtype:V3 interneuron.description: V3 interneurons are a class of excitatory glutamatergic neurons in the ventral spinal cord that arise from the Nkx2-2-expressing p3 progenitor domain. They play a critical role in establishing robust and balanced locomotor rhythms by providing excitatory drive to motor circuits. In the E9.5–E10.0 mouse embryo, these neurons are among the early-born ventral interneuron populations undergoing active differentiation and axon pathfinding.

type:Telencephalon.name: Telencephalon
type:Telencephalon.description: The telencephalon is the most anterior division of the embryonic forebrain, giving rise to the cerebral cortex, hippocampus, basal ganglia, and olfactory bulb. At E8.5–E10.0, this population represents early telencephalic neuroepithelial progenitors that are actively expanding and beginning to regionalize along dorsoventral and anteroposterior axes.

topLinks.explanation: The eye field and telencephalon both arise from the anterior neural plate/prosencephalic neuroectoderm, sharing a common forebrain progenitor pool in which the single eye field is initially specified as a medial domain contiguous with the prospective telencephalon before separating.

The diencephalon and telencephalon are both prosencephalon (forebrain) derivatives arising from a common pool of anterior neural plate/neuroectoderm progenitors, so their strong shared ancestry simply reflects their origin from the same regionalized forebrain neuroepithelium.

Both the hypothalamus and telencephalon derive from the prosencephalon (anterior forebrain) of the rostral neural plate, sharing SIX3/SIX6/FOXG1-expressing anterior neuroectoderm progenitors that co-emerge during forebrain regionalization.

Hypothalamic neurons (diencephalic) and telencephalon are sister subdivisions of the prosencephalon, both arising from a common anterior neural plate/forebrain neuroectoderm progenitor pool that splits during forebrain regionalization.

Midbrain neurons and telencephalon both derive from the anterior neuroectoderm/neural plate, tracing back to a shared pool of early anterior neural progenitors that only later become regionalized along the antero-posterior axis into forebrain and midbrain.

subtype:Telencephalon (dorsal).name: Telencephalon (dorsal)
subtype:Telencephalon (dorsal).description: Dorsal telencephalic progenitors constitute the precursors of the cerebral cortex (pallium), including future neocortex and hippocampus. Arising from the anterior neural plate by E8.5, these cells form the dorsal wall of the telencephalic vesicles and are characterized by a proliferative neuroepithelium that will generate the layered cortical projection neurons in later development.

subtype:Telencephalon (ventral).name: Telencephalon (ventral)
subtype:Telencephalon (ventral).description: The ventral telencephalon (subpallium) comprises progenitor cells of the ganglionic eminences and preoptic area in the developing mouse forebrain, emerging from E9.0 onward. These progenitors give rise to GABAergic interneurons and basal ganglia projection neurons, and are patterned by ventralizing morphogen signals including Shh from the underlying mesenchyme and ventral midline.

type:Epibranchial placode.name: Epibranchial placode
type:Epibranchial placode.description: Epibranchial placodes are transient ectodermal thickenings that arise adjacent to the pharyngeal (branchial) clefts during mid-embryogenesis. They generate the sensory neurons of the geniculate, petrosal, and nodose cranial ganglia (cranial nerves VII, IX, and X), which relay visceral sensory information including taste and cardiorespiratory afferents. Their appearance from E8.5 through E10.0 aligns with the progressive formation and delamination of neuroblasts from these placodes during pharyngeal arch development.

topLinks.explanation: Epibranchial sensory neurons are the direct differentiated progeny of the epibranchial placodes, which are ectodermal thickenings that delaminate to form the distal (geniculate, petrosal, nodose) cranial sensory ganglion neurons, so the two share a direct placodal progenitor lineage.

Both cell types derive from the non-neural surface ectoderm, with epibranchial placodes emerging from the posterior pre-placodal region at the neural plate border that is lineally continuous with the general epidermal ectoderm, so they share a common surface-ectoderm progenitor pool.

Epibranchial placodes are thickenings that delaminate directly from the non-neural surface (cranial) ectoderm via the pan-placodal ectoderm, so both cell types descend from a shared surface-ectoderm progenitor pool at the neural plate border.

Both are cranial neurogenic placodes that arise from the common pre-placodal ectoderm (a Six1/Eya-expressing band at the anterior neural plate border), so they share a recent progenitor pool within this placodal domain before segregating into trigeminal versus epibranchial (geniculate/petrosal/nodose) fates.

Both are epiblast-derived non-neural/surface ectoderm derivatives, so their shared ancestry likely reflects a common pool of early surface-ectoderm progenitors (the non-neural ectoderm domain from which the amnion and the neural-plate-border preplacodal ectoderm giving rise to epibranchial placodes both segregate).

type:Epibranchial sensory neuron.name: Epibranchial sensory neuron
type:Epibranchial sensory neuron.description: Epibranchial sensory neurons are visceral sensory neurons derived from the epibranchial placodes (geniculate, petrosal, and nodose), which delaminate from the surface ectoderm to populate cranial ganglia VII, IX, and X. These neurons relay taste, cardiovascular, and visceral organ information to the brainstem and are among the earliest placode-derived neurons to differentiate, consistent with their appearance from E9.0 onward. Their surface ectoderm lineage reflects their placodal rather than neural crest origin.

topLinks.explanation: Epibranchial sensory neurons are the direct differentiated progeny of the epibranchial placodes, which are ectodermal thickenings that delaminate to form the distal (geniculate, petrosal, nodose) cranial sensory ganglion neurons, so the two share a direct placodal progenitor lineage.

Epibranchial sensory neurons delaminate from epibranchial placodes, which arise from the same non-neural/surface (preplacodal) ectoderm that gives rise to epidermal progenitors, so both share a common surface-ectoderm progenitor pool at the neural plate border.

Both cell types derive from the common preplacodal ectoderm at the cranial neural-plate border, where the trigeminal and epibranchial placodes (the latter giving rise to epibranchial sensory neurons) emerge from a shared cranial placodal progenitor field.

Both cell types arise from the common posterior cranial pre-placodal ectoderm—specifically the Pax2/Pax8+ otic-epibranchial progenitor domain (OEPD)—which co-generates the otic placode and the epibranchial placodes that give rise to epibranchial sensory neurons.

Both are neurogenic cranial-placode derivatives that emerge from the shared otic-epibranchial progenitor domain (OEPD) within the posterior preplacodal ectoderm, so their sensory neurons descend from a common Pax2/Foxi-expressing placodal progenitor pool.

type:Epidermal progenitor.name: Epidermal progenitor
type:Epidermal progenitor.description: Epidermal progenitors are surface ectoderm cells that have committed to an epidermal fate and will give rise to the stratified epithelium of the skin. Emerging from E8.5 onward, these progenitors express the master transcription factor p63 (Trp63), which drives the stratified epithelial program, and progressively establish the basal layer of the developing epidermis. They also serve as a signaling center, secreting growth factors that pattern the underlying dermal mesenchyme.

topLinks.explanation: Epidermal progenitors are the direct descendants of surface (non-neural) ectoderm, which is specified by BMP-driven lineage restriction of the ectodermal epiblast, so the two cell types are essentially sequential stages of the same surface-ectoderm-to-epidermis lineage.

Both cell types derive from the non-neural surface ectoderm, with epibranchial placodes emerging from the posterior pre-placodal region at the neural plate border that is lineally continuous with the general epidermal ectoderm, so they share a common surface-ectoderm progenitor pool.

Epibranchial sensory neurons delaminate from epibranchial placodes, which arise from the same non-neural/surface (preplacodal) ectoderm that gives rise to epidermal progenitors, so both share a common surface-ectoderm progenitor pool at the neural plate border.

Both cell types derive from the same surface (non-neural) ectoderm progenitor pool—the lens placode is a local thickening of head surface ectoderm, the same epithelium that produces epidermal progenitors—so their shared ancestry reflects a common surface-ectoderm origin.

Both derive from cranial surface (non-neural) ectoderm—epidermal progenitors from the general surface ectoderm and trigeminal sensory neurons from the neurogenic placodes (ophthalmic/maxillomandibular trigeminal placodes) that bud off the adjacent preplacodal ectoderm at the neural-plate border, giving them a recent shared ectodermal progenitor pool.

subtype:Epidermal progenitor (anterior).name: Epidermal progenitor (anterior)
subtype:Epidermal progenitor (anterior).description: Epidermal progenitors (anterior) are surface ectoderm-derived cells that give rise to the epidermis and associated ectodermal appendages of the head and face during mid-gestation mouse development. Emerging from E9.0 onward, these progenitors express the stratification master regulator Trp63 and epithelial markers such as Epcam and Krt18, while carrying a positional identity that aligns them with craniofacial and anterior ectodermal fates. They contribute to the developing facial prominences, oral ectoderm, and anterior surface structures.

subtype:Epidermal progenitor (posterior).name: Epidermal progenitor (posterior)
subtype:Epidermal progenitor (posterior).description: Epidermal progenitors (posterior) are surface ectoderm-derived epithelial cells located in the posterior (trunk and caudal) regions of the mouse embryo. Emerging from E8.5 onward, these cells form the outer epithelial covering of the embryo and will ultimately give rise to the stratified epidermis and its appendages in posterior body segments. They share a core epidermal identity with other surface ectoderm populations but are distinguished by their posterior axial position.

type:Lens placode.name: Lens placode
type:Lens placode.description: The lens placode is a thickened ectodermal epithelium overlying the optic vesicle that invaginates between E9.5 and E10.0 to form the lens pit and subsequently the lens vesicle, the precursor of the crystalline lens. Induced by signals from the underlying optic vesicle and surrounding mesenchyme, it is one of the cranial sensory placodes derived from the pre-placodal region of the surface ectoderm.

topLinks.explanation: The lens and olfactory placodes both arise from the pan-placodal (preplacodal) ectoderm, a horseshoe-shaped domain of cranial non-neural ectoderm bordering the anterior neural plate, so their shared ancestry reflects a common cranial placode progenitor field.

Both cell types arise from the cranial pre-placodal ectoderm at the anterior neural-plate border—the lens placode from the ophthalmic/lens region and trigeminal sensory neurons from the adjacent ophthalmic and maxillomandibular trigeminal placodes—so they share a common non-neural cranial ectoderm progenitor pool.

Both the lens and trigeminal placodes arise from the same common progenitor field, the cranial preplacodal ectoderm (a Six1/Eya-expressing horseshoe of ectoderm bordering the anterior neural plate) that segregates into individual placodes, so their shared ancestry reflects this common panplacodal origin.

Both cell types derive from the same surface (non-neural) ectoderm progenitor pool—the lens placode is a local thickening of head surface ectoderm, the same epithelium that produces epidermal progenitors—so their shared ancestry reflects a common surface-ectoderm origin.

Both derive from the anterior cranial placode region of the preplacodal ectoderm (the panplacodal primordium bordering the anterior neural plate), with lens placode and olfactory placode arising as neighboring anterior placodes from this shared progenitor domain.

type:Olfactory placode.name: Olfactory placode
type:Olfactory placode.description: The olfactory placode is a bilateral thickening of the cranial surface ectoderm that emerges around E9.0 in the mouse and gives rise to the olfactory epithelium, including olfactory sensory neurons and their supporting cells. It is one of the earliest sensory placodes to be specified and later invaginates to form the olfactory pit, which matures into the nasal cavity lining responsible for odor detection.

topLinks.explanation: The olfactory placode is the cranial ectodermal thickening that directly generates olfactory sensory neurons, so both cell types derive from the same placodal progenitor pool in a direct progenitor-to-progeny lineage.

The lens and olfactory placodes both arise from the pan-placodal (preplacodal) ectoderm, a horseshoe-shaped domain of cranial non-neural ectoderm bordering the anterior neural plate, so their shared ancestry reflects a common cranial placode progenitor field.

Both are cranial placodes derived from the same preplacodal ectoderm (panplacodal primordium) at the anterior neural plate border, which subsequently segregates into individual placodes, so their shared ancestry reflects this common placodal progenitor field.

Both cell types derive from the non-neural surface ectoderm—the olfactory placode arises from the anterior preplacodal ectoderm at the neural plate border, a specialized domain of the same surface ectoderm that gives rise to epidermal progenitors—so they share a recent common ectodermal progenitor pool.

Both derive from the preplacodal ectoderm at the anterior neural plate border—the olfactory placode directly, and trigeminal sensory neurons in part from the placodally-derived (ophthalmic/maxillomandibular) neurons of the trigeminal ganglion—so they share a common cranial placode/preplacodal progenitor field.

type:Olfactory sensory neuron.name: Olfactory sensory neuron
type:Olfactory sensory neuron.description: Olfactory sensory neurons are the primary chemosensory neurons of the nasal epithelium, responsible for detecting odorants and transmitting signals to the olfactory bulb. They arise from the olfactory placode, a surface ectoderm-derived thickening that begins neurogenesis around E9.5 in the mouse, consistent with their appearance at E9.5–E10.0 in this dataset.

topLinks.explanation: The olfactory placode is the cranial ectodermal thickening that directly generates olfactory sensory neurons, so both cell types derive from the same placodal progenitor pool in a direct progenitor-to-progeny lineage.

Both derive from the anterior cranial placode region of the preplacodal ectoderm (the panplacodal primordium bordering the anterior neural plate), with lens placode and olfactory placode arising as neighboring anterior placodes from this shared progenitor domain.

Both olfactory sensory neurons (olfactory placode-derived) and the trigeminal placode arise from the common anterior pre-placodal ectoderm (PPE) at the neural plate border, sharing a cranial placodal progenitor field before segregating into individual placodes.

Both derive from the non-neural surface (cranial) ectoderm—olfactory sensory neurons arise from the olfactory placode, an ectodermal placode that buds from the same surface ectoderm sheet that generates epidermal progenitors, so they share a recent common ectodermal progenitor pool in the anterior head region.

Frontonasal mesenchyme (cranial neural crest) and olfactory sensory neurons (olfactory placode) likely share ancestry because both derive from the anterior neural plate border and co-emerge within the rostral frontonasal/nasal region, so lineage-tracing captures their common origin in the anterior head progenitor pool.

type:Otic placode.name: Otic placode
type:Otic placode.description: The otic placode is a thickened ectodermal epithelium adjacent to the hindbrain that invaginates to form the otic vesicle (otocyst), the precursor of the entire inner ear including the cochlea and vestibular apparatus. Arising from the pre-placodal ectoderm around E8.0–E8.5 in mouse, it undergoes progressive morphogenesis through E9.5–E10.0, giving rise to the sensory, non-sensory, and neurogenic compartments of the developing inner ear.

topLinks.explanation: Otic sensory (statoacoustic ganglion) neurons delaminate directly from the otic placode/vesicle, so both cell types descend from the same cranial placodal progenitor pool.

Both are cranial sensory placodes that arise from the common pre-placodal ectoderm (panplacodal primordium) at the anterior neural plate border, so they share a recent progenitor field before segregating into individual placodes.

Both cell types arise from the common posterior cranial pre-placodal ectoderm—specifically the Pax2/Pax8+ otic-epibranchial progenitor domain (OEPD)—which co-generates the otic placode and the epibranchial placodes that give rise to epibranchial sensory neurons.

Both are cranial (posterior) placodes that arise from the common preplacodal ectoderm at the anterior neural plate border, sharing the posterior placodal area/otic-epibranchial progenitor field induced by FGF signaling.

Both cell types derive from surface (non-neural) ectoderm—the otic placode arises from the preplacodal ectoderm at the neural plate border, the same surface-ectoderm sheet that gives rise to epidermis, so they share a common ectodermal progenitor pool.

type:Otic sensory neuron.name: Otic sensory neuron
type:Otic sensory neuron.description: Otic sensory neurons are bipolar neurons that delaminate from the neurogenic region of the otic vesicle (developing inner ear) and coalesce to form the cochleovestibular ganglion (cranial nerve VIII). These neurons relay auditory and vestibular information from sensory hair cells to the brainstem. Their appearance at E9.0–E10.0 corresponds to the window of neuroblast delamination and early ganglion formation in mouse development.

topLinks.explanation: Otic sensory (statoacoustic ganglion) neurons delaminate directly from the otic placode/vesicle, so both cell types descend from the same cranial placodal progenitor pool.

Both derive from the cranial preplacodal ectoderm (PPE) surrounding the anterior neural plate—the otic placode giving rise to otic sensory neurons and the trigeminal (ophthalmic/maxillomandibular) placode—so they share a common placodal progenitor domain.

Both are neurogenic cranial-placode derivatives that emerge from the shared otic-epibranchial progenitor domain (OEPD) within the posterior preplacodal ectoderm, so their sensory neurons descend from a common Pax2/Foxi-expressing placodal progenitor pool.

Both cell types arise from surface (non-neural) ectoderm—epidermal progenitors directly, and otic sensory neurons via the otic placode that delaminates from preplacodal/surface ectoderm adjacent to the hindbrain—so they share a common ectodermal progenitor pool.

Both cell types arise from the preplacodal ectoderm via a shared otic-epibranchial progenitor domain (OEPD), a common Pax2/Pax8/Sox3+ posterior placodal field that segregates into otic placode–derived (vestibulocochlear) and epibranchial placode–derived sensory neurons.

type:Pre-placodal ectoderm.name: Pre-placodal ectoderm
type:Pre-placodal ectoderm.description: Pre-placodal ectoderm is a horseshoe-shaped domain of surface ectoderm that borders the anterior neural plate and gives rise to all cranial sensory placodes, including the olfactory, lens, otic, and epibranchial placodes. Present at E8.5–E9.0, this progenitor field is specified by the intersection of BMP attenuation, FGF, and retinoic acid signaling at the neural plate border, and represents a transient competence state before individual placodes become specified.

type:Surface ectoderm.name: Surface ectoderm
type:Surface ectoderm.description: Surface ectoderm is the non-neural portion of the embryonic ectoderm that covers the outer surface of the embryo after neurulation. It gives rise to the epidermis, hair follicles, sensory placodes, and associated glands, and plays critical signaling roles in patterning underlying mesenchyme during craniofacial and limb development.

topLinks.explanation: Epidermal progenitors are the direct descendants of surface (non-neural) ectoderm, which is specified by BMP-driven lineage restriction of the ectodermal epiblast, so the two cell types are essentially sequential stages of the same surface-ectoderm-to-epidermis lineage.

Both are non-neural squamous ectodermal epithelia derived from the pluripotent epiblast, with amniotic ectoderm arising from posterior/proximal epiblast adjacent to the primitive streak and surface (non-neural) ectoderm from embryonic ectoderm, so they share a recent common epiblast-derived progenitor pool.

Epibranchial placodes are thickenings that delaminate directly from the non-neural surface (cranial) ectoderm via the pan-placodal ectoderm, so both cell types descend from a shared surface-ectoderm progenitor pool at the neural plate border.

Epibranchial sensory neurons delaminate from epibranchial placodes, which are focal thickenings of cranial surface ectoderm derived from the preplacodal/panplacodal ectoderm, so both cell types share a common surface-ectodermal progenitor pool.

The lens placode is a focal thickening that delaminates directly from the head surface ectoderm (induced by the underlying optic vesicle), so both cell types descend from the same surface/non-neural ectoderm progenitor pool.

subtype:Apical ectodermal ridge.name: Apical ectodermal ridge
subtype:Apical ectodermal ridge.description: The apical ectodermal ridge (AER) is a specialized thickened epithelial structure that forms at the distal tip of the developing limb bud, serving as a critical signaling center for limb outgrowth and proximal-distal patterning. It secretes FGF ligands that maintain the underlying mesenchyme in a proliferative, undifferentiated state, and its appearance at E9.5–E10.0 coincides with the onset of forelimb and hindlimb bud emergence in the mouse.

subtype:Surface ectoderm (anterior).name: Surface ectoderm (anterior)
subtype:Surface ectoderm (anterior).description: Surface ectoderm (anterior) is the non-neural ectoderm overlying the rostral (head) region of the mouse embryo during early organogenesis. This epithelial tissue gives rise to the anterior epidermis and contributes to cranial sensory placodes, including the lens and olfactory placodes. Present from E8.0 through E9.0, it represents the anterior domain of the surface ectoderm as it becomes regionalized along the body axis.

subtype:Surface ectoderm (posterior).name: Surface ectoderm (posterior)
subtype:Surface ectoderm (posterior).description: Surface ectoderm (posterior) is the non-neural ectoderm overlying the caudal (trunk and tail) region of the mouse embryo, present from E8.0 through E10.0 as the body axis elongates. This epithelial population will give rise to the posterior epidermis and contributes to dorsal–ventral patterning of underlying tissues through secreted signals such as WNT6. It is distinguished from anterior surface ectoderm by its expression of posterior positional identity genes rather than cranial or placodal programs.

type:Trigeminal placode.name: Trigeminal placode
type:Trigeminal placode.description: The trigeminal placode is a region of thickened surface ectoderm in the developing head that gives rise to somatosensory neurons of the trigeminal (cranial nerve V) ganglion, which mediates touch, pain, and temperature sensation across the face and jaw. Appearing from E9.0 onward in this dataset, these cells are undergoing specification and delamination from the surface ectoderm to contribute the placode-derived neuronal population of the trigeminal ganglion, complementing the neural crest-derived component. As part of the surface ectoderm lineage, trigeminal placode cells retain epithelial characteristics while activating a neurogenic program.

topLinks.explanation: The trigeminal placode is the cranial ectodermal progenitor that directly delaminates and differentiates into trigeminal (distal) sensory neurons of the trigeminal ganglion, so the two represent sequential stages of a single placodal neurogenic lineage.

Both the lens and trigeminal placodes arise from the same common progenitor field, the cranial preplacodal ectoderm (a Six1/Eya-expressing horseshoe of ectoderm bordering the anterior neural plate) that segregates into individual placodes, so their shared ancestry reflects this common panplacodal origin.

Both are cranial sensory placodes that arise from the common pre-placodal ectoderm (panplacodal primordium) at the anterior neural plate border, so they share a recent progenitor field before segregating into individual placodes.

Both derive from the cranial preplacodal ectoderm (PPE) surrounding the anterior neural plate—the otic placode giving rise to otic sensory neurons and the trigeminal (ophthalmic/maxillomandibular) placode—so they share a common placodal progenitor domain.

Both are cranial placodes derived from the same preplacodal ectoderm (panplacodal primordium) at the anterior neural plate border, which subsequently segregates into individual placodes, so their shared ancestry reflects this common placodal progenitor field.

type:Trigeminal sensory neuron.name: Trigeminal sensory neuron
type:Trigeminal sensory neuron.description: Trigeminal sensory neurons are somatosensory neurons of the trigeminal ganglion (cranial nerve V) that innervate the face, jaw, and anterior head to relay touch, pain, and temperature signals. In the mouse embryo, a major population of these neurons derives from the trigeminal placode, a thickened region of surface ectoderm, consistent with the ectoderm/surface ectoderm lineage assignment. These neurons are among the earliest born sensory neurons, appearing from E9.0 onward as the trigeminal ganglion coalesces and extends peripheral and central projections.

topLinks.explanation: Both cell types arise from the cranial pre-placodal ectoderm at the anterior neural-plate border—the lens placode from the ophthalmic/lens region and trigeminal sensory neurons from the adjacent ophthalmic and maxillomandibular trigeminal placodes—so they share a common non-neural cranial ectoderm progenitor pool.

The trigeminal placode is the cranial ectodermal progenitor that directly delaminates and differentiates into trigeminal (distal) sensory neurons of the trigeminal ganglion, so the two represent sequential stages of a single placodal neurogenic lineage.

Both derive from cranial surface (non-neural) ectoderm—epidermal progenitors from the general surface ectoderm and trigeminal sensory neurons from the neurogenic placodes (ophthalmic/maxillomandibular trigeminal placodes) that bud off the adjacent preplacodal ectoderm at the neural-plate border, giving them a recent shared ectodermal progenitor pool.

Both derive from the preplacodal ectoderm at the anterior neural plate border—the olfactory placode directly, and trigeminal sensory neurons in part from the placodally-derived (ophthalmic/maxillomandibular) neurons of the trigeminal ganglion—so they share a common cranial placode/preplacodal progenitor field.

Both are cranial sensory neurons derived from neurogenic ectodermal placodes arising from the common pre-placodal region (the trigeminal/ophthalmic-maxillomandibular placode and the epibranchial placodes), giving them a shared placodal progenitor origin.

type:Autonomic neuron.name: Autonomic neuron
type:Autonomic neuron.description: Autonomic neurons are neural crest-derived neurons that give rise to the sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric divisions of the autonomic nervous system. Emerging at E9.5–E10.0, these cells have delaminated from the neural crest, migrated to target sites such as the sympathetic ganglia, and begun terminal neuronal differentiation, as reflected by their expression of neurofilament genes and cell cycle exit markers.

topLinks.explanation: Autonomic neurons are the direct differentiated progeny of autonomic progenitors—both derive from the neural crest/sympathoadrenal lineage (e.g., trunk neural crest–derived sympathoblasts), so the progenitor-to-neuron transition within a single clone produces their strong shared ancestry.

Autonomic neurons derive directly from neural crest, and vagal neural crest is the specific migratory progenitor population that seeds parasympathetic and enteric autonomic neurons, so they represent successive stages of one continuous lineage.

Both cell types derive from trunk neural crest cells, which delaminate from the dorsal neural tube and give rise to sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia as well as sympathetic/autonomic neurons of the peripheral nervous system.

Both derive from trunk neural crest cells, which delaminate from the dorsal neural tube and migrate to give rise to sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia and to autonomic (sympathetic/parasympathetic) neurons, so they share a common multipotent neural crest progenitor pool.
